NKJV.1: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
NKJV.2: “Command the children of Israel that they bring to you pure oil of pressed olives for the light, to make the lamps burn continually.
NKJV.3: Outside the veil of the Testimony, in the tabernacle of meeting, Aaron shall be in charge of it from evening until morning before the LORD continually; it shall be a statute forever in your generations.
NKJV.4: He shall be in charge of the lamps on the pure gold lampstand before the LORD continually.
NKJV.5: “And you shall take fine flour and bake twelve cakes with it. Two-tenths of an ephah shall be in each cake.
NKJV.6: You shall set them in two rows, six in a row, on the pure gold table before the LORD.
NKJV.7: And you shall put pure frankincense on each row, that it may be on the bread for a memorial, an offering made by fire to the LORD.
NKJV.8: Every Sabbath he shall set it in order before the LORD continually, being taken from the children of Israel by an everlasting covenant.
NKJV.9: And it shall be for Aaron and his sons, and they shall eat it in a holy place; for it is most holy to him from the offerings of the LORD made by fire, by a perpetual statute.”
NKJV.10: Now the son of an Israelite woman, whose father was an Egyptian, went out among the children of Israel; and this Israelite woman’s son and a man of Israel fought each other in the camp.
NKJV.11: And the Israelite woman’s son blasphemed the name of the LORD and cursed; and so they brought him to Moses. (His mother’s name was Shelomith the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.)
NKJV.12: Then they put him in custody, that the mind of the LORD might be shown to them.
NKJV.13: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
NKJV.14: “Take outside the camp him who has cursed; then let all who heard him lay their hands on his head, and let all the congregation stone him.
NKJV.15: “Then you shall speak to the children of Israel, saying: ‘Whoever curses his God shall bear his sin.
NKJV.16: And whoever blasphemes the name of the LORD shall surely be put to death. All the congregation shall certainly stone him, the stranger as well as him who is born in the land. When he blasphemes the name of the LORD, he shall be put to death.
NKJV.17: ‘Whoever kills any man shall surely be put to death.
NKJV.18: Whoever kills an animal shall make it good, animal for animal.
NKJV.19: ‘If a man causes disfigurement of his neighbor, as he has done, so shall it be done to him—
NKJV.20: fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth; as he has caused disfigurement of a man, so shall it be done to him.
NKJV.21: And whoever kills an animal shall restore it; but whoever kills a man shall be put to death.
NKJV.22: You shall have the same law for the stranger and for one from your own country; for I am the LORD your God.’ ”
NKJV.23: Then Moses spoke to the children of Israel; and they took outside the camp him who had cursed, and stoned him with stones. So the children of Israel did as the LORD commanded Moses.

NASB.1: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
NASB.2: 'Command the sons of Israel that they bring to you clear oil from beaten olives for the light, to make a lamp burn continually.
NASB.3: 'Outside the veil of testimony in the tent of meeting, Aaron shall keep it in order from evening to morning before the LORD continually; [it shall be] a perpetual statute throughout your generations.
NASB.4: 'He shall keep the lamps in order on the pure [gold] lampstand before the LORD continually.
NASB.5: 'Then you shall take fine flour and bake twelve cakes with it; two-tenths [of an ephah] shall be [in] each cake.
NASB.6: 'You shall set them [in] two rows, six [to] a row, on the pure [gold] table before the LORD.
NASB.7: 'You shall put pure frankincense on each row that it may be a memorial portion for the bread, [even] an offering by fire to the LORD.
NASB.8: 'Every sabbath day he shall set it in order before the LORD continually; it is an everlasting covenant for the sons of Israel.
NASB.9: 'It shall be for Aaron and his sons, and they shall eat it in a holy place; for it is most holy to him from the LORD'S offerings by fire, [his] portion forever.'
NASB.10: Now the son of an Israelite woman, whose father was an Egyptian, went out among the sons of Israel; and the Israelite woman's son and a man of Israel struggled with each other in the camp.
NASB.11: The son of the Israelite woman blasphemed the Name and cursed. So they brought him to Moses. (Now his mother's name was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.)
NASB.12: They put him in custody so that the command of the LORD might be made clear to them.
NASB.13: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
NASB.14: 'Bring the one who has cursed outside the camp, and let all who heard him lay their hands on his head; then let all the congregation stone him.
NASB.15: 'You shall speak to the sons of Israel, saying, 'If anyone curses his God, then he will bear his sin.
NASB.16: 'Moreover, the one who blasphemes the name of the LORD shall surely be put to death; all the congregation shall certainly stone him. The alien as well as the native, when he blasphemes the Name, shall be put to death.
NASB.17: 'If a man takes the life of any human being, he shall surely be put to death.
NASB.18: 'The one who takes the life of an animal shall make it good, life for life.
NASB.19: 'If a man injures his neighbor, just as he has done, so it shall be done to him:
NASB.20: fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth; just as he has injured a man, so it shall be inflicted on him.
NASB.21: 'Thus the one who kills an animal shall make it good, but the one who kills a man shall be put to death.
NASB.22: 'There shall be one standard for you; it shall be for the stranger as well as the native, for I am the LORD your God.''
NASB.23: Then Moses spoke to the sons of Israel, and they brought the one who had cursed outside the camp and stoned him with stones. Thus the sons of Israel did, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

ESV.1: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
ESV.2: “Command the people of Israel to bring you pure oil from beaten olives for the lamp, that a light may be kept burning regularly.
ESV.3: Outside the veil of the testimony, in the tent of meeting, Aaron shall arrange it from evening to morning before the LORD regularly. It shall be a statute forever throughout your generations.
ESV.4: He shall arrange the lamps on the lampstand of pure gold  before the LORD regularly.
ESV.5: “You shall take fine flour and bake twelve loaves from it; two tenths of an ephah  shall be in each loaf.
ESV.6: And you shall set them in two piles, six in a pile, on the table of pure gold  before the LORD.
ESV.7: And you shall put pure frankincense on each pile, that it may go with the bread as a memorial portion as a food offering to the LORD.
ESV.8: Every Sabbath day Aaron shall arrange it before the LORD regularly; it is from the people of Israel as a covenant forever.
ESV.9: And it shall be for Aaron and his sons, and they shall eat it in a holy place, since it is for him a most holy portion out of the LORD's food offerings, a perpetual due.”
ESV.10: Now an Israelite woman's son, whose father was an Egyptian, went out among the people of Israel. And the Israelite woman's son and a man of Israel fought in the camp,
ESV.11: and the Israelite woman's son blasphemed the Name, and cursed. Then they brought him to Moses. His mother's name was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.
ESV.12: And they put him in custody, till the will of the LORD should be clear to them.
ESV.13: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
ESV.14: “Bring out of the camp the one who cursed, and let all who heard him lay their hands on his head, and let all the congregation stone him.
ESV.15: And speak to the people of Israel, saying, Whoever curses his God shall bear his sin.
ESV.16: Whoever blasphemes the name of the LORD shall surely be put to death. All the congregation shall stone him. The sojourner as well as the native, when he blasphemes the Name, shall be put to death.
ESV.17: “Whoever takes a human life shall surely be put to death.
ESV.18: Whoever takes an animal's life shall make it good, life for life.
ESV.19: If anyone injures his neighbor, as he has done it shall be done to him,
ESV.20: fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth; whatever injury he has given a person shall be given to him.
ESV.21: Whoever kills an animal shall make it good, and whoever kills a person shall be put to death.
ESV.22: You shall have the same rule for the sojourner and for the native, for I am the LORD your God.”
ESV.23: So Moses spoke to the people of Israel, and they brought out of the camp the one who had cursed and stoned him with stones. Thus the people of Israel did as the LORD commanded Moses.

NLT.2: “Command the people of Israel to bring you pure oil of pressed olives for the light, to keep the lamps burning continually.
NLT.3: This is the lampstand that stands in the Tabernacle, in front of the inner curtain that shields the Ark of the Covenant. Aaron must keep the lamps burning in the LORD’s presence all night. This is a permanent law for you, and it must be observed from generation to generation.
NLT.4: Aaron and the priests must tend the lamps on the pure gold lampstand continually in the LORD’s presence.
NLT.5: “You must bake twelve flat loaves of bread from choice flour, using four quarts of flour for each loaf.
NLT.6: Place the bread before the LORD on the pure gold table, and arrange the loaves in two stacks, with six loaves in each stack.
NLT.7: Put some pure frankincense near each stack to serve as a representative offering, a special gift presented to the LORD.
NLT.8: Every Sabbath day this bread must be laid out before the LORD as a gift from the Israelites; it is an ongoing expression of the eternal covenant.
NLT.9: The loaves of bread will belong to Aaron and his descendants, who must eat them in a sacred place, for they are most holy. It is the permanent right of the priests to claim this portion of the special gifts presented to the LORD.”
NLT.10: One day a man who had an Israelite mother and an Egyptian father came out of his tent and got into a fight with one of the Israelite men.
NLT.11: During the fight, this son of an Israelite woman blasphemed the Name of the LORD with a curse. So the man was brought to Moses for judgment. His mother was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri of the tribe of Dan.
NLT.12: They kept the man in custody until the LORD’s will in the matter should become clear to them.
NLT.13: Then the LORD said to Moses,
NLT.14: “Take the blasphemer outside the camp, and tell all those who heard the curse to lay their hands on his head. Then let the entire community stone him to death.
NLT.15: Say to the people of Israel: Those who curse their God will be punished for their sin.
NLT.16: Anyone who blasphemes the Name of the LORD must be stoned to death by the whole community of Israel. Any native-born Israelite or foreigner among you who blasphemes the Name of the LORD must be put to death.
NLT.17: “Anyone who takes another person’s life must be put to death.
NLT.18: “Anyone who kills another person’s animal must pay for it in full — a live animal for the animal that was killed.
NLT.19: “Anyone who injures another person must be dealt with according to the injury inflicted —
NLT.20: a fracture for a fracture, an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth. Whatever anyone does to injure another person must be paid back in kind.
NLT.21: “Whoever kills an animal must pay for it in full, but whoever kills another person must be put to death.
NLT.22: “This same standard applies both to native-born Israelites and to the foreigners living among you. I am the LORD your God.”
NLT.23: After Moses gave all these instructions to the Israelites, they took the blasphemer outside the camp and stoned him to death. The Israelites did just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

AMP.1: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
AMP.2: "Command the children of Israel to bring to you clear oil from beaten olives for the light [of the golden lampstand], to make a lamp burn continually.
AMP.3: Outside the veil of the Testimony [between the Holy Place and the Most Holy Place] in the Tent of Meeting, Aaron shall always keep the lamps burning before the LORD from evening until morning; it shall be a permanent statute throughout your generations.
AMP.4: He shall keep the lamps burning on the pure gold lampstand before the LORD continually.
AMP.5: "Then you shall take fine flour and bake twelve cakes (bread of the Presence, showbread) with it; two-tenths of an ephah shall be in each cake (loaf).
AMP.6: You shall set the bread of the Presence (showbread) in two rows, six in a row, on the pure gold table before the LORD.
AMP.7: You shall put pure frankincense [in two censers, one] beside each row, so that it may be with the bread as a memorial portion, an offering by fire to the LORD.
AMP.8: Every Sabbath day Aaron shall arrange the showbread before the LORD continually; it is an everlasting covenant for the Israelites.
AMP.9: The bread of the Presence shall be for Aaron and his sons, and they shall eat it in a sacred place, for it is for Aaron a most holy portion of the offerings by fire to the LORD, his portion forever."
AMP.10: Now the son of an Israelite woman, whose father was an Egyptian, went out among the Israelites, and he and a man of Israel quarreled and struggled with each other in the camp.
AMP.11: The Israelite woman's son blasphemed the Name [of the LORD] and cursed. So they brought him to Moses. (Now his mother's name was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.)
AMP.12: They put him in custody until the will and command of the LORD might be made clear to them.
AMP.13: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
AMP.14: "Bring the one who has cursed [the LORD] outside the camp, and let all who heard him lay their hands on his head [as witnesses to his guilt]; then let all the congregation stone him.
AMP.15: You shall speak to the Israelites, saying, 'Whoever curses his God will bear his sin [through his own death].
AMP.16: Further, the one who blasphemes the name of the LORD shall most certainly be put to death; all the congregation shall stone him. The stranger as well as the native-born shall be put to death when he blasphemes the Name [of the LORD].
AMP.17: 'If a man takes the life of any human being [unlawfully], he shall most certainly be put to death.
AMP.18: The one who kills an animal shall replace it, animal for animal.
AMP.19: If a man injures his neighbor (fellow citizen), whatever he has done shall be done to him:
AMP.20: fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth; just as he has injured a man, so shall the same be done to him.
AMP.21: The one who kills an animal shall replace it; but he who kills a human being [unlawfully] shall be put to death.
AMP.22: You shall have one standard of law for the stranger among you as well as for the native, for I am the LORD your God.'"
AMP.23: Then Moses spoke to the Israelites, and they brought the one who had cursed [the LORD] outside the camp and stoned him with stones. Thus the Israelites did just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

NRSVCE.1: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
NRSVCE.2: Command the people of Israel to bring you pure oil of beaten olives for the lamp, that a light may be kept burning regularly.
NRSVCE.3: Aaron shall set it up in the tent of meeting, outside the curtain of the covenant, to burn from evening to morning before the LORD regularly; it shall be a statute forever throughout your generations.
NRSVCE.4: He shall set up the lamps on the lampstand of pure gold before the LORD regularly.
NRSVCE.5: You shall take choice flour, and bake twelve loaves of it; two-tenths of an ephah shall be in each loaf.
NRSVCE.6: You shall place them in two rows, six in a row, on the table of pure gold.
NRSVCE.7: You shall put pure frankincense with each row, to be a token offering for the bread, as an offering by fire to the LORD.
NRSVCE.8: Every sabbath day Aaron shall set them in order before the LORD regularly as a commitment of the people of Israel, as a covenant forever.
NRSVCE.9: They shall be for Aaron and his descendants, who shall eat them in a holy place, for they are most holy portions for him from the offerings by fire to the LORD, a perpetual due.
NRSVCE.10: A man whose mother was an Israelite and whose father was an Egyptian came out among the people of Israel; and the Israelite woman’s son and a certain Israelite began fighting in the camp.
NRSVCE.11: The Israelite woman’s son blasphemed the Name in a curse. And they brought him to Moses — now his mother’s name was Shelomith, daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan —
NRSVCE.12: and they put him in custody, until the decision of the LORD should be made clear to them.
NRSVCE.13: The LORD said to Moses, saying:
NRSVCE.14: Take the blasphemer outside the camp; and let all who were within hearing lay their hands on his head, and let the whole congregation stone him.
NRSVCE.15: And speak to the people of Israel, saying: Anyone who curses God shall bear the sin.
NRSVCE.16: One who blasphemes the name of the LORD shall be put to death; the whole congregation shall stone the blasphemer. Aliens as well as citizens, when they blaspheme the Name, shall be put to death.

NRSVCE.18: Anyone who kills an animal shall make restitution for it, life for life.

NIV.1:
Oil and Bread Set Before the Lord
The Lord said to Moses,
NIV.2: “Command the Israelites to bring you clear oil of pressed olives for the light so that the lamps may be kept burning continually.
NIV.3: Outside the curtain of the Testimony in the Tent of Meeting, Aaron is to tend the lamps before the Lord from evening till morning, continually. This is to be a lasting ordinance for the generations to come.
NIV.4: The lamps on the pure gold lampstand before the Lord must be tended continually.
NIV.5: “Take fine flour and bake twelve loaves of bread, using two-tenths of an ephah for each loaf.
NIV.6: Set them in two rows, six in each row, on the table of pure gold before the Lord.
NIV.7: Along each row put some pure incense as a memorial portion to represent the bread and to be an offering made to the Lord by fire.
NIV.8: This bread is to be set out before the Lord regularly, Sabbath after Sabbath, on behalf of the Israelites, as a lasting covenant.
NIV.9: It belongs to Aaron and his sons, who are to eat it in a holy place, because it is a most holy part of their regular share of the offerings made to the Lord by fire.”
NIV.10:
A Blasphemer Stoned
Now the son of an Israelite mother and an Egyptian father went out among the Israelites, and a fight broke out in the camp between him and an Israelite.
NIV.11: The son of the Israelite woman blasphemed the Name with a curse; so they brought him to Moses. (His mother’s name was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri the Danite.)
NIV.12: They put him in custody until the will of the Lord should be made clear to them.
NIV.13: Then the Lord said to Moses:
NIV.14: “Take the blasphemer outside the camp. All those who heard him are to lay their hands on his head, and the entire assembly is to stone him.
NIV.15: Say to the Israelites: ‘If anyone curses his God, he will be held responsible;
NIV.16: anyone who blasphemes the name of the Lord must be put to death. The entire assembly must stone him. Whether an alien or native-born, when he blasphemes the Name, he must be put to death.
NIV.17: “‘If anyone takes the life of a human being, he must be put to death.
NIV.18: Anyone who takes the life of someone’s animal must make restitution—life for life.
NIV.19: If anyone injures his neighbor, whatever he has done must be done to him:
NIV.20: fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth. As he has injured the other, so he is to be injured.
NIV.21: Whoever kills an animal must make restitution, but whoever kills a man must be put to death.
NIV.22: You are to have the same law for the alien and the native-born. I am the Lord your God.’”
NIV.23: Then Moses spoke to the Israelites, and they took the blasphemer outside the camp and stoned him. The Israelites did as the Lord commanded Moses.
